# rmux 0.1.12 — preview
This release polishes search, tab renaming, and project context.
## Everyday navigation
- File-preview search finds literal text in reading order. - Tab renaming shows the name limit and keeps overlong drafts available for correction. Closing another tab preserves the draft and focus. - Text fields preserve modified shortcuts and reset horizontal scrolling correctly when text becomes shorter.
## Project context
- Local terminals can explicitly look up pull requests using an existing authenticated GitHub CLI. The sidebar shows the result and opens its link; pending lookups can be canceled from the command palette. - Port summaries retain the last explicit scan and identify partial snapshots. - New terminal histories use one atomic initial write, reducing startup disk work. - The browser demo shares the desktop branch/directory row and keeps sample directories consistent across tabs, splits, and sample `pwd` output.
## Downloads and validation
GitHub builds the signed and notarized macOS Apple Silicon DMG and ZIP, Linux x86-64 tarball, and Windows x86-64 ZIP. macOS updates use Sparkle. The [browser demo](https://rmux.app) runs bundled sample sessions, without shell or server access.
Focused tests and desktop compilation passed during development. Browser checks covered tab-renaming focus and close behavior. Native visual review and Windows runtime validation remain pending.
Use rmux alongside VS Code with its built-in external-terminal shortcut: [setup guide](https://rmux.app/vscode/).
